A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete 30-page documents including Appendices A–C. Text comparison and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the methods, equations, figures, references and proofs.

before.justification: v4 reports original experiments in Section 6, including toy optimization, MNIST, CIFAR10/100 coreset training and Mushrooms semi-supervised logistic regression, with outcomes in Figures 1–10.

after.justification: v5 retains the original experiments and outcomes in Section 6 and Figures 1–10. These remain original empirical results despite being unchanged from v4.

M1.justification: AuxMOM and AuxMVR retain the same update rules in Equations 5–6. The appendix algorithms, alternative AuxMOM variant and decentralized helper procedures are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same toy problem, MNIST rotation/mislabeling and coreset tasks, CIFAR10/100 coreset tasks, and Mushrooms semi-supervised logistic regression. No evaluated coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Section 6 and Figures 1–10 retain the same experiment-specific comparators, including Naive, Fine Tuning and SGDm controls. The coreset comparison arms also match.

E3.justification: The reported protocols match, including MNIST batch sizes of 256 for f and 64 for h, coreset sampling proportions, the three equal Mushrooms partitions and stepsize grid search. Metrics, models and evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 1–6 and 9 retain the same analyses of gradient bias, Hessian similarity, local-step count, rotations, incorrect labels and coreset size. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: The existing shaded bands, including those in Figures 7–9, are identical. Neither version specifies repeated-run or seed counts, and v5 adds no uncertainty-estimation details or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 1–10 contain identical plotted results, and Section 6 retains the same numerical summaries and qualitative findings. No result entries are added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: The assumptions, convergence theorems, corollaries and derivations match. Appendices B–C retain the same lemmas, counterexample and proofs, including the extension to multiple decentralized helpers.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same framework and two-algorithm contributions, convergence-rate claims under Hessian similarity, and potential benefit from correlated gradient noise.

C2.justification: The interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including uncertainty about Hessian similarity in practical applications, fine-tuning's reusable pretraining advantage, and the unresolved construction of positively correlated gradient noise.

D1.justification: Both versions provide the same architecture descriptions, hyperparameters, data-processing information and algorithm pseudocode. Appendix A retains the same code-access statement and repository address.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the relationships to SVRG, DANE, MiMe and auxiliary learning. The reference lists match.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v4, dated 24 Feb 2024, to v5, dated 18 Dec 2025. Apart from negligible spacing differences, the prose, terminology, section order and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: All ten figures retain the same graphics, axes, legends, captions and placement. Algorithm and theorem displays, section pagination and overall page layout are also retained.

improvement.justification: v5 preserves the same scientific content, experimental evidence, proofs, limitations and reproducibility information, including the appendices. The updated version/date stamp and negligible typesetting differences do not materially improve or weaken the paper's rigor, completeness or readability.
